package_info.why_malicious: All Vuetify versions prior to 2.1.9 are vulnerable to a Cross-site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability via the error-messages array. This allows attackers to inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript into the UI, leading to code execution in the user's browser. The vulnerability is present in the core rendering logic of the package and can be exploited by untrusted user input.

execution_context.file_location: Vue component template using Vuetify's v-text-field with :error-messages binding

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code binds the error-messages prop of v-text-field to a user-controlled array (tweetErrors), which can contain unsanitized user input. When an error is triggered (e.g., tweet text > 280 chars), the user's input is inserted into the error-messages array and rendered as HTML, allowing execution of embedded JavaScript (e.g., via ).

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Rendering user-controlled input as HTML without sanitization enables XSS attacks, allowing arbitrary JavaScript execution in the user's browser.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, error messages should be sanitized or escaped before rendering to prevent code execution. Here, user input is rendered directly as HTML.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would involve rendering static or sanitized error messages, not direct user input.
key_indicators: Direct binding of user input to error-messages prop
Lack of input sanitization or escaping
Ability to inject HTML/JavaScript via user input

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the user enters text longer than 280 characters, the code pushes a string containing the raw user input (shareTwitterText) into the tweetErrors array, which is then rendered unsanitized in the UI, enabling XSS if the input contains HTML/JavaScript.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Directly embedding user input into error messages without sanitization is a classic XSS vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Error messages should not include unsanitized user input, especially when rendered as HTML.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Echoing user input in error messages is common, but should always be escaped.
key_indicators: String interpolation of user input in error message
No sanitization or escaping before rendering
Error message displayed via vulnerable error-messages prop

attack_chain.action: User enters malicious input (e.g., ) into the tweet text field.
attack_chain.leads_to: Input is stored in the shareTwitterText variable.

attack_chain.action: User clicks the Share on Twitter button; if the input exceeds 280 characters, the shareTwitter method pushes an error message containing the raw input into tweetErrors.
attack_chain.leads_to: tweetErrors array contains unsanitized user input.

attack_chain.action: The v-text-field component renders the error-messages prop, displaying the malicious input as HTML in the DOM.
attack_chain.leads_to: Injected JavaScript executes in the user's browser (XSS).

behavioral_signatures: Rendering user-controlled input as HTML in error or status messages
Direct binding of user input to UI component props that render HTML
Lack of input sanitization or escaping in error message construction
file_indicators: Vue components using :error-messages or similar props with user input
String interpolation of user input in error messages
network_indicators: N/A (XSS is a client-side attack; no direct network indicators unless used for further exploitation)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Statically analyze Vue components for usage of :error-messages, :messages, or similar props bound to variables that may contain user input. Flag cases where user input is interpolated into error/status messages without sanitization. At runtime, monitor for DOM insertion of unsanitized user input, especially in error or status message areas. Automated testing can attempt to inject HTML/JavaScript payloads into input fields and observe if they are executed.
